source: Theorem (Dominated Convergence Theorem): Let $(f_n)$ be measurable functions on a measure space such that $f_n \to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n| \le g$ for some integrable function $g \in L^1$. Then $f \in L^1$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} \int |f_n-f| = 0$, hence $\lim_{n \to \infty} \int f_n = \int f$.

source: Defintion: A function $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is Riemann integrble if there exists $I \in \mathbb{R}$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a partition $P$ with upper sum $U(f,P)$ and lower sum $L(f,P)$ satisfying $U(f,P)-L(f,P)<\varepsilon$, and then $I=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$.
